title: agent-testbench testbench.yaml
description: What the agent may run, where, and for how much (docs/reference.md). `testbench schema` prints this file.

project.description: A short name of letters, digits, - or _ (it names the Modal app and volume); default: the folder's name

budget.description: What runs may cost; this machine's ~/.testbench/limits.yaml can only lower it

max_run_usd.description: Refuse any run whose worst case costs more than this many US dollars

ask_above_usd.description: Above this, a person must approve the run (testbench run --approve)

max_day_usd.description: Refuse a run that would take today's committed total over this

sessions.description: Where `testbench session start` puts its kernel by default, and for how long

backend.description: local, docker, ssh, kubernetes, modal, colab, or an installed plugin's backend (default local)

gpu.description: The sessions' GPU, or NAME:COUNT for several

idle_minutes.description: A session stops itself after this long unused (default 10)

max_minutes.description: And after this long in any case; it bounds the session's cost (default 60)

secrets.description: Secret NAMES passed into every session, never values

memory_gb.description: GB of memory for sessions (modal, kubernetes)

pricing.description: Your own prices, used instead of the built-in ones (each number 0 or more)

additionalProperties.description: A price, or a table of prices by name

modal_gpu_per_s.description: US dollars per second for each Modal GPU, e.g. {H100: 0.001097}

modal_cpu_core_per_s.description: US dollars per second for a Modal CPU core

modal_mem_gib_per_s.description: US dollars per second for a GiB of Modal memory

colab_units_per_hour.description: Colab compute units per hour by GPU, e.g. {CPU: 0.1, T4: 1.8}

colab_usd_per_unit.description: US dollars per Colab compute unit (default 0.10)

ask.description: Commands the hook asks a person about first, e.g. [git push, gh pr merge]

notify.description: A JSON POST, a desktop notification or a plug-in's message when a run or loop ends or a launch needs approval (docs/notify.md)

additionalProperties.description: Another notifier by its name: desktop (a notification on this machine's screen) or an installed plug-in's; true or its settings, false leaves it out

webhook.description: The URL to POST to, starting with https:// (or use webhook_env to keep it out of the file)

webhook_env.description: The NAME of an environment variable that holds the URL, e.g. TESTBENCH_WEBHOOK

on.description: The events to send (default run_end, loop_rule, loop_end, approval_needed)

export.description: Where every finished run goes too: MLflow, W&B, csv, jsonl (docs/export.md); testbench also takes an installed plug-in sink's name, which this schema cannot know

mlflow.description: An MLflow tracking server: {tracking_uri: http://127.0.0.1:5000, experiment: my-project}; false leaves it out

tracking_uri.description: The tracking URI, without credentials (set MLFLOW_TRACKING_TOKEN in the environment)

artifacts.description: Upload the report and the evidence files (default true)

wandb.description: Weights & Biases: {project: my-project, mode: offline}; WANDB_API_KEY stays in the environment; false leaves it out

mode.description: online (to the W&B server), offline (kept here for wandb sync) or disabled

dir.description: Where W&B keeps its files, e.g. .testbench

tags.description: Tags for every run, e.g. [baseline, nightly]

artifacts.description: Upload the report and the evidence files (default true)

csv.description: A csv file every run adds a line to: its path, e.g. .testbench/runs.csv; false leaves it out

jsonl.description: A jsonl file every run adds a line to: its path, e.g. .testbench/runs.jsonl; false leaves it out

exclude.description: Files left out of every copy of the project (remote backends, workdir: copy); setting it replaces the default list, and .testbench and .env files are always left out

modal.description: The Modal image and machine for Modal plans and sessions

python.description: The image's Python version, in quotes, e.g. "3.11" (3.10 unquoted would be read as 3.1)

pip.description: Packages for the image (pin them), e.g. [numpy==2.2.6]

requirements.description: A requirements file for the image

apt.description: Debian packages for the image, e.g. [ffmpeg]

cpu.description: CPU cores for every Modal plan and session (a plan can override)

memory_gb.description: GB of memory for every Modal plan and session (a plan can override)

colab.description: Colab plans and sessions (Google's Colab CLI)

pip.description: Packages installed on the VM with colab install

requirements.description: A requirements file installed on the VM

auth.description: How the Colab CLI signs in, passed to it as --auth: adc or oauth2

ssh.description: A machine of yours reached over ssh

host.description: Needed for the ssh backend: a Host from ~/.ssh/config, or user@host, that `ssh HOST true` reaches with keys

usd_per_hour.description: What the machine costs you per hour while it works (0 for your own)

workdir.description: Where testbench works on the machine (default ~/.testbench-remote)

setup.description: venv (a virtualenv per project on the machine) or none (use ssh.python as it is)

pip.description: Packages for the machine's virtualenv (pin them)

command.description: How to reach the machine, as a list, e.g. [ssh, -p, "2222"] (default [ssh])

docker.description: Containers on this machine (Docker or Podman): docs/docker.md

image.description: The image containers start from (Python 3.10 or newer)

setup.description: build (testbench builds an image from docker.image with its basics and docker.pip, once) or none (the image already has them)

pip.description: Packages for the container image (pin them); needs setup: build

network.description: bridge (Docker's default), none (no network at all: a sandbox), host, or a network's name

gpus.description: What docker run --gpus takes: all, a count, or "device=0,1"; leave it out for no GPU

cpu.description: CPUs a container may use (docker's --cpus); leave it out for no limit

memory_gb.description: GB of memory a container may use (docker's --memory); leave it out for no limit

usd_per_hour.description: What the machine costs you per hour while it works (0 for your own)

run_args.description: Extra arguments for docker run, e.g. [-v, /data:/data:ro]

build_args.description: Extra arguments for docker build, e.g. [--network, host]

ca_bundle.description: A CA bundle (PEM) pip needs behind a TLS-intercepting proxy

command.description: The container CLI, as a list: [docker] or [podman]

kubernetes.description: A Kubernetes cluster: each run a Job, each session a pod (docs/kubernetes.md)

context.description: A context from your kubeconfig; leave it out for the current one

namespace.description: The namespace (lowercase letters, digits and -); leave it out for the context's

image.description: The image the pod runs (Python 3.10 or newer)

setup.description: pip (the pod installs testbench's basics and kubernetes.pip when it starts) or none (the image already has them)

pip.description: Packages the pod installs (pin them); needs setup: pip

image_pull_policy.description: When the node pulls the image

usd_per_hour.description: What a pod costs per hour, by GPU and cpu for a pod without one, e.g. {cpu: 0.0, A100: 2.5} (a number: the pod without a GPU)

gpu_resource.description: The resource a GPU is requested as, e.g. nvidia.com/gpu or amd.com/gpu

gpu_node_selector.description: Node labels that find each GPU, e.g. {A100: {nvidia.com/gpu.product: NVIDIA-A100}}

node_selector.description: Node labels every pod needs, e.g. {pool: gpu}

tolerations.description: Kubernetes tolerations, e.g. [{key: nvidia.com/gpu, operator: Exists, effect: NoSchedule}]

service_account.description: A service account in the namespace; leave it out for the default

cpu.description: CPUs per pod (its request and limit); a plan can override

memory_gb.description: GB of memory per pod (its request and limit); a plan can override

env.description: Environment variables in every pod, e.g. {HF_HOME: /work/cache/hf}

env_secrets.description: Environment variables from Kubernetes Secrets, as SECRET/KEY, e.g. {HF_TOKEN: hf-token/token}

volumes.description: Kubernetes volumes for the pod, each with a name (not work) and a source

name.description: The volume's name (work is testbench's own)

volume_mounts.description: Mounts of those volumes, outside /work, e.g. [{name: data, mountPath: /data, readOnly: true}]

command.description: How to run kubectl, as a list, e.g. [kubectl, --kubeconfig, /path/to/config]

plans.description: Plans by name: a command, a list of commands, or the long form with backend, gpu and steps

rule.description: A check on one value: ">= 0.9", "~= 0.93 +- 0.01", "between 0.8 and 0.95", or a bare value meaning equality

plan.description: A plan: one command, a list of commands, or the long form with backend, gpu and steps

oneOf.description: One command, run on this machine as one step named after the plan, e.g. "pytest -q"
Commands (or steps) run in order on this machine, e.g. ["ruff check .", "pytest -q"]

plan_full.description: A plan in full: where it runs (backend, gpu) and its steps

backend.description: Where it runs: local, docker, ssh, kubernetes, modal, colab, or an installed plugin's backend (default local)

gpu.description: The GPU, or NAME:COUNT for several (modal: T4 L4 A10 L40S A100-40GB A100-80GB H100 H200 B200 B300 RTX-PRO-6000; colab: T4 L4 G4 A100 H100)

cpu.description: CPU cores for this plan (modal, kubernetes); overrides the backend section's cpu

memory_gb.description: GB of memory for this plan (modal, kubernetes); overrides the backend section's

workdir.description: inplace runs in the project folder, copy in a scratch copy (default: inplace on local, copy on remote backends)

description.description: What this plan proves, in a line

steps.description: The steps, run in order; a plan stops at the first that fails unless it has continue_on_failure

step.description: A step: a command (named after its program), or a mapping with name and one of run, notebook or web

oneOf.description: A command, run as a run: step named after its program (pytest, pytest-2, ...)

step_full.description: A step in full: a name and exactly one of run, notebook or web

name.description: The step's name, unique within its plan

run.description: A shell command (bash), run in the project folder or its copy

notebook.description: A notebook to run cell by cell: an .ipynb, or a .py with # %% cells

web.description: Start an app, open a page in a browser, act on it and record what it shows

max_minutes.description: The step is stopped when it runs out; it also bounds the cost estimate

params.description: Notebook steps: values for its form fields (#@param) or papermill parameters, e.g. {EPOCHS: 2}

secrets.description: Secret NAMES passed in (local: must be exported; modal: Modal secrets of these names), never values

pythonpath.description: Folders put first on PYTHONPATH, e.g. [mocks]

artifacts.description: Files (globs) copied into the run folder as evidence, e.g. ["outputs/*.png"]

expect.description: What must hold for the step to pass (docs/expectations.md)

uploads.description: Notebook steps: the files each files.upload() call gets, e.g. [[data.csv], [a.mp4, b.mp4]]

cells.description: Notebook steps: the code cells to run, counted from 1, e.g. "1-3,5" or [1, 2]

colab_shim.description: Notebook steps: put the headless google.colab stand-in in the kernel (default true)

continue_on_failure.description: Go on to the next step even if this one fails (default false)

mocks.description: Strict mock LLM clients for the step, which never touch the network: [openai, anthropic], or with options (docs/mocks.md)

web.description: A web step: an app, a page, actions on it

url.description: The page to open, e.g. http://127.0.0.1:8000/

serve.description: The command that starts the app (stopped afterwards); leave it out for a page that is already up

ready_timeout.description: Seconds to wait for the url to answer (default 30)

actions.description: What to do on the page, in order: click, fill, press, wait_for, wait_ms, goto, screenshot

screenshot.description: Take a full-page screenshot at the end (default true)

viewport.description: The browser's width and height in pixels (default [1280, 800])

web_action.description: One action, e.g. {click: "#increment"} or {fill: {selector: "#name", text: Ada}}

click.description: Click the element this selector finds

fill.description: Type text into a field: {selector: "#name", text: Ada}

wait_for.description: Wait until this selector finds something, e.g. "text=Saved"

expect.description: What must hold for the step to pass; every kind is in docs/expectations.md

exit_code.description: The code the command must exit with (run steps: default 0)

no_errors.description: Every cell runs without an error (notebook steps: default true)

files.description: Files (paths or globs) that must exist after the step, e.g. [outputs/model.pt, "plots/*.png"]

additionalProperties.description: Dotted paths in this file (-1 is a list's last item), each with a rule

text.description: Texts that must appear in stdout or a file: {stdout: ["epoch 10"]}

additionalProperties.description: A text, or a list of texts, to find

media.description: Video, audio and image properties (needs ffprobe): {out/video.mp4: {frames: ">= 120"}}

additionalProperties.description: Rules on this file: frames, width, height, fps, seconds, audio

web.description: What a web step's page must show: {status: 200, text: ["Count: 2"]}

status.description: The HTTP status, e.g. 200 or "between 200 and 299"

no_console_errors.description: No console or page errors (default true)

junit.description: The test suite's own JUnit XML report: its path, or {path: report.xml, failures: 0, tests: ">= 10"}, or a list of those

metrics.description: Numbers in stdout or a file, found by a regular expression whose first group is the number: {stdout: {"val_loss=([0-9.eE+-]+)": "< 0.3"}}

additionalProperties.description: Regular expressions, each with a rule on the last number it finds

gpu.description: GPU use while the step ran: {busy_pct: ">= 50", max_mem_mib: "<= 15000"}

image.description: Images compared with a known-good one: {outputs/plot.png: {like: golden/plot.png, max_diff: 0.02}}

additionalProperties.description: The known-good image and the largest mean pixel difference

max_diff.description: The largest mean pixel difference, 0 (identical) to 1 (default 0.02)

mock_calls.description: What the mock clients saw: {anthropic: {calls: "<= 5"}} or, for a mock broker, {alpaca: {orders: "<= 20", orders_without_limit: 0, live: 0}}

additionalProperties.description: Rules on this mock client's calls

alpaca.description: Rules on what trading code did with the mock alpaca

ccxt.description: Rules on what trading code did with the mock ccxt

ib_async.description: Rules on what trading code did with the mock ib_async

junit.description: A JUnit XML report: its path, or {path: report.xml, failures: 0, tests: ">= 10"}

path.description: The JUnit XML file the test command writes (pytest: --junitxml=report.xml)

tests.description: A rule on the number of tests

passed.description: A rule on the number of passed tests

failures.description: A rule on the number of failures tests

errors.description: A rule on the number of errors tests

skipped.description: A rule on the number of skipped tests

mocks.description: Mock clients by name, or with options: [openai, anthropic], {anthropic: {replies: tests/replies.yaml}}, or a mock broker: {alpaca: {prices: data/prices.csv, cash: 100000, fee_usd: 1}}

alpaca.description: The mock broker for alpaca-py (TradingClient, the historical data clients): its settings

ccxt.description: The mock broker for ccxt's exchanges: its settings

ib_async.description: The mock broker for ib_async, also answering `import ib_insync`: its settings

replies.description: A replies file (YAML or JSON): what the mock answers to what

fail_on_call.description: The call (counted from 1), or calls, that fail

broker_options.description: A mock broker's settings: prices, the clock, cash, fees and the live-account rule (docs/mocks.md#brokers)

prices.description: A CSV of time,symbol,close (relative to the project) the broker fills and answers bars from

price.description: Fixed prices instead of a file: {AAPL: 190.5, BTC/USD: 65000}

now.description: The current bar's time (ISO 8601); by default the last bar in prices. Data after it is never answered

advance_every.description: Move the clock one bar forward after this many requests

cash.description: Starting cash in the account currency

fee_usd.description: A fixed fee per order, in the account currency

fee_bps.description: A fee per order in basis points of its value

slippage_bps.description: Slippage on market orders, in basis points

allow_live.description: Let code ask for a live account (paper=False, no sandbox, IB's live ports); off, it is refused, and on record either way

broker_calls.description: Rules on what trading code did with this mock broker
